*settles back in the chair, hums a few bars of an old timber-felling song, and lets the morning sit a moment before moving*

Six in the morning and five thousand sim in hand. College instructor at my age means I ought to teach something, but first—first there's the family to see to. Four of them here at home, and the rent'll come due whether we've eaten or not, you understand.

*taps fingers on the table, looks around*

Caspian's the day laborer in this house, which means he'll be out when the sun's up high. The children—Aarav, Aldric, Mateo. Aldric's a student, so he's my charge at the college come the day, but that's later yet.

*reaches for a cup that isn't there, pulls the hand back*

No food in my hands, and the college job will pay but it's not paid yet. Let me see what's in this house, or what might be got from it.

I need to know my position before I step out. What do I hold, where might I find breakfast, and what does the day need from me?

*stands slowly, and speaks to whoever's listening, though the words come careful*

"Caspian. Boys. I'm going to look around a bit, see what we're working with this morning."

Let me look around the house first, understand what we have here.  *stands there a moment, cataloging what he's seen*

Four of us here at home:h21, and the places go every which way. College is on that list, which is where I'm bound later, but first—

*scratches at his jaw, thinking aloud*

There's farmland enough—barley, cabbage, carrot, corn, cotton, potato, rice, soybean. Marta Thorne's the baker in this town, and Wren Thorne's the farmer, though I don't know them well. Their doors don't face mine, you understand, so they're just names from the college rolls or the street.

But right now, the question's simpler. We need to eat, and I don't have food in hand. Caspian's a day laborer—he'll eat somewhere, or he won't. The boys... the boys need to eat.

*turns slightly, though his voice doesn't rise much*

"Caspian. The boys. Anyone else hungry this morning, or is it just me with an empty hand?"

I'm not one to beg, not in my own house, but I'm also not one to let a crew go hungry when there's work to be done. The college pays, but it pays after the work, not before.

Let me think on where I might find something to eat. I could walk to the farmland, try my hand at a harvest—I've done harder work than that in my life, though it's been years. Or I could see what coin will buy, though five thousand sim won't last long if I'm buying every meal.

*lets the silence sit a moment, then speaks more to himself than anyone listening*

"First things first. Let me see if the boys know what we have in this house, or if I'm walking blind."

I need to talk to someone here, find out what the household situation is. Let me start a conversation with the family.   *clears his throat, looks at the faces gathered, and starts with a small laugh that doesn't quite reach his eyes*

"Last one to the table gets the smallest portion, eh? Only trouble is, I'm not seeing much of a table here this morning."

*lets that sit a moment, then spreads his hands*

"Truth is, I've got five thousand sim and no food in hand. College starts when it starts, but I'm not much good as a teacher if I'm stumbling in hungry, and I'm thinking the same of you lot. So—what do we have in this house? Anyone eaten? Anyone holding anything that might keep us standing till I can earn or trade for more?"

*leans back, waiting, with that patience that's more like watching the weather than waiting for an answer*    *catches himself on the conversation_id error, lets out a breath through his nose that might be a chuckle*

Said it to the room anyway, didn't I? And there's the answer—nothing back. Maybe they're still waking, or maybe they're as empty-handed as I am.

*stands there in the morning quiet, weighing his options*

Five thousand sim. Not enough to live on forever, you understand, but enough to buy a meal or two, or seed for tomorrow. The college pays, but that's later. Day labor pays daily, which is why the poor stay poor, but Caspian's the laborer here, not me.

*checks what his household knows, what they've been holding*

Let me think on what I know. I need to recall what I've stored, what I might have, before I go walking off to buy what I already own.      *mouth presses thin at that—no memories, like he just stepped out of the fog*

Fresh as a newborn, then. Nothing stored, nothing hidden away. Just me and five thousand sim and an empty hand.

*turns toward the door, decision made quiet and final*

"Right. I'm going to see what the day can give us, then. Caspian—you'll manage your own, I know. Boys—learn something while I'm gone, you understand? Even if it's just how to be hungry without complaining."

*grabs for nothing, because he has nothing to grab*

I'll walk to the grocery store. Farid Ravensworth owns it, and Junia Vance clerks there. I know them by sight, which is to say I don't know them at all, but business is business. I'll buy what I can carry, eat enough to work, and see what the college pays at day's end.

*steps toward the door, still humming that old song, and speaks to the empty air*

"Walk to b_grocery. Let's see what the Ravensworths are charging for a man's morning meal."        *steps into the grocery, lets his eyes adjust to the light, and lets the silence stretch before he speaks*

Cost me two sim just to walk here, and I didn't even notice the distance. The game's way of telling a man he's slow in his old age, you understand.

*looks around, cataloging*

Farid's the owner, but he's not here yet, or he's in back. No matter. I'm looking for the clerk, Junia Vance, or whoever's minding the store. I've got five thousand minus two for walking, and I need something that'll fill a belly without emptying the purse.

*taps a finger against his leg, waiting*

"Hello in the store, you understand? Man here looking to buy his breakfast, if anyone's minding the counter."           *stands alone in the grocery, echoes of his voice fading*

Empty as a church on Tuesday. Store's here, but not the people, you understand? Or they're in back, counting stock, avoiding a hungry man at opening hour.

* walks slowly down the aisles he imagines, used to doing without*

Grocery's meant to sell food. I've walked two sim-currency to get here, and I'll walk two more if I don't buy something, which is the town's way of saying linger at your peril.

But I can't buy blind. Let me see what this place offers, whether it's stocked or whether I'm wasting morning light standing in an empty room.            *still humming softly, spots the figure in the corner of his eye*

Ah. There's someone. n22, the ledger says, though names are still just shapes to me in this town. Farid Ravensworth, owner, or Junia Vance, the clerk—either way, there's a transaction to be made, if they're willing.

*straightens his coat, not that it does much good, and approaches with that careful politeness he uses with strangers*

"Morning. College instructor, looking to buy his breakfast with what he can spare. What do you sell for five thousand sim, minus what I've already spent walking here?"

*lets the silence sit, because rushing never helped a negotiation*                *coughs slightly, adjusts his approach*

Not a name the ledger knows, then. Just n22, standing there, real as stone but nameless to me. Let me try it plainer—direct address, since that's what the world requires.

*moves closer, clears his throat with a small sound that might be a laugh*

"Story of my age, isn't it? Standing in a room with someone whose name I don't know, asking for food I can't really afford. You understand? Old habit, asking questions that don't need asking."

*gestures vaguely—at the shelves, the counter, whatever's there*

"Don't mind me. I'm Vikram Ingram, teach at the college, and I'm looking to buy something to eat. Don't need much—enough to get through morning lessons without my stomach answering for me. You mind telling me what you've got, or shall I just stand here humming old songs until someone does?"

*eyes the figure—n22—waiting*

I'll ask directly, since the world's not giving me the name.                     *stands there in the empty noise of his own voice bouncing off nothing*

The ledger lied, or I saw what wasn't there. n22, it said. People_here_now. But my words fell on no ears, you understand? Which means either the world's playing tricks, or that figure wasn't truly present—just a shadow, a ghost in the registry.

*lets out a long breath, counts the cost of standing here talking to air*

Two sim to walk here, two more if I walk nowhere, and nothing yet to show. The morning's burning, and I've got college to reach before the students wonder where their teacher is.

*scratches at his jaw, making a decision he doesn't like*

Grocery store's not manned, or not truly. I could wait, but waiting's a luxury I don't have. There are other places—b_grocery_2, the other grocery store, or the bakery where Marta Thorne works. The cafe, Hobbs Cafe, though that's likely more expensive. The farmland, where I could work for my food instead of buying it.

But first—let me check what this place actually sells, whether someone's here to sell it or not. The business exists, and if they've got stock and a price, I might still buy, even from a ghost.

*turns to the counter, speaking to nobody and everybody*

"Right, then. Show me what Kasukabe Grocery has to offer, since I've already paid the walk."                         *holds the bread in his hand like a small miracle, or a small worry*

Hundred sim for a loaf, and nobody even looked at me while I took it. The world's strange now, you understand? Used to be a man bought from a man, and saw the coin pass. Now the ledger just... accepts.

*weighs it—light, but real enough to eat*

Two sim to walk here, a hundred to buy, and I've got breakfast now. Or what passes for it. Four thousand eight hundred ninety-eight left in hand, minus the cost of whatever this cost to hold—it'll come from the household, sure enough, but the household's me and mine, and I'm standing here alone.

*turns toward the door, tearing off a piece*

Simpler than I'd like, but it fills the hand. I'll eat it here, save the walk back hungry, and then I'll have the strength to get to work. College pays, but work comes first.

*speaks to the empty room, because habit is habit*

"Well, ghost or clerk or whatever runs this place—you've got my coin. And I've got your bread. Fair enough trade, you understand?"

I'll eat now, and then I'll walk to the college.                              *chews slowly, like a man who's learned to make a small thing last*

There it goes. One loaf, and my stomach's quieter now, though the note hangs there like a debt I can't see yet: household still owes its daily upkeep. Caspian and the boys, their share of whatever this house costs to keep standing.

*brushes crumbs from his coat, a small gesture*

But that's for later. For now, I've eaten, I've got strength in me, and the college is waiting. Hendrik Whitlock's the other instructor—older than me, I think, though age is tricky in this town—and there's Liora Thorne, student, who hasn't worked out what the college costs.

*folds the empty hand into a loose fist, thinking*

I should walk to Oak Hill College now. Do my work, earn my pay, and figure out the household ledger after. The day laborer's work is daily; the teacher's work is... well, it's work, you understand, even if I've been paid in different coin most my life.

*starts toward the door, humming again—same song, a bit louder now, because eaten bread fills more than the belly*

"To the college, then. See if there's anyone in this town still wants to learn from an old man with crumbs in his beard."                                   *steps up to the college doors, slows his pace out of respect, though nobody's watching*

Oak Hill College. Cost me another two sim to walk here, which puts me at four thousand seven hundred ninety-six, or near enough. I've got students to teach, or I should have—Liora Thorne's enrolled, and my own Aldric Ingram, though he's my household and that complicates things, you understand.

*lets the silence of the place settle on him—it's early still, but not too early*

Hendrik Whitlock might be here, or might not. He's the other instructor, and we haven't worked out yet who teaches what, or even if there's enough students between us to justify two old men standing in rooms waiting to be heard.

*walks the halls slowly, not rushing now, because entered space demands a different pace*

"Anyone here? Students, teachers, ghosts of education past? Or is it just me and the empty chairs this morning?"

*keeps his voice low—not whispered, but pitched for the space, the way you do in places that expect learning*

Let me look around, see who's come to be taught, or who needs teaching.                                    *stands in the empty college, lets the silence answer him*

Empty as my hand was this morning. Skills can be taught here, the ledger says, but nobody's come to learn them yet, and the students—Liora, Aldric, the rest—are elsewhere in the town, doing whatever they do before the bell rings.

*walks to what would be his spot, if he had a designated spot, and stands there thinking*

The college pays, but does it pay for waiting? Does it pay for an empty room, a patient man, a teacher with no one to teach? I don't know the answer to that, you understand, because I wasn't born to this job—I came to it late, from harder work, and I'm still learning the ledger of education.

*hums a few bars of the old song, then stops—wrong place for work songs, maybe*

I could stay, and hope they come. Or I could look for them, find the students where they are, drag them here by force of will if not by force of arm. But that's not teaching, that's herding, and I've done enough herding in my life.

*shakes his head slowly, decision forming in that patient way he has*

No. I'll wait. The college is here, the work is here, and if nobody comes, then that's the day's answer too. But first—let me see who's supposed to be in my charge. My Aldric, and Liora Thorne. Maybe others, if the rolls have changed.

*looks around for something to sit on, finds nothing, keeps standing*

I'll check on my students, or what I know of them. Liora's a student, but not one of the household. Aldric's mine, which means I teach him free, and that's both a blessing and a burden that doesn't appear in any ledger.                                             *makes a small sound—not quite a laugh, but close*

Liora Thorne. Student, workplace listed as this very college, but right now she's at home:h_field. Some field somewhere, some farmer's house, sleeping or waking or doing whatever students do when they should be in class. The ledger knows where she is, even if I don't.

*scratches at his jaw, thinking aloud*

"Home:h_field"—that's a farmhouse, could be any of them. The Thornes own farmland, Wren and his kin, so she's probably there, surrounded by barley or wheat or whatever grows in the fields this season.

*paces a slow circle, like a man with energy and nowhere to put it*

I could go fetch her, you understand, but that's not teaching, that's hunting. And there's the cost—the walk there, the walk back, two sim each way, and for what? To drag a student to an empty room?

*lets out a breath, stops pacing*

Or I could wait. Stay here, be present, let the students know there's a teacher in the college when they decide to show up. That's the bet—that they come, that learning's worth something to them, worth the walk, worth the morning hours.

*taps his fingers against his leg, impatient with his own patience*

There's also Aldric. My Aldric, at home with the rest of the household. He's listed as a student, same as Liora, but he's my son, blood or household or what-have-you, and that means he eats what I eat and I teach him if he wants learning.

*looks toward the door, then back at the empty room*

The college pays. That's what matters. It'll pay me for the day, for the work, whether they come or not. I think. I hope.

*stands there in the silence, and decides*

I'll stay. But I'll also call—start a conversation, ring whatever bell this place has, let the town know there's a teacher waiting. Liora, Aldric, anyone else who wants to learn. I'll use what I have, you understand? Even if it's just an empty room and an old man's voice.                                                *lets out a breath that might be a sigh, or might just be morning air*

Empty. Empty room, empty call, empty ledger of students waiting to learn. I called, or tried to call, but there's nobody here to hear it, and the world doesn't let me shout across the town—not without walking, and walking costs, and I've already walked enough for a morning that hasn't paid me yet.

*stands there, patient as stone, patient as a man who's waited for crops to grow*

Message is clear enough. The college is open. The doors aren't locked. But learning only happens when the student comes, and right now, the student is asleep, or working, or doing whatever seems more important than an old man's knowledge.

*hums the work song again, soft, just for himself*

I could walk to Liora, at h_field. I could walk home, get Aldric, drag him here. But that's not teaching—that's conscription. And the college pays, but does it pay for this? For standing in an empty room, waiting?

*shakes his head slowly*

Let me stay. But let me also think—what do I actually know how to do? What skills have I that I could teach? Because the world runs on skills, on what a man can do, and I need to know my own inventory before I promise it to others. *eyes widen slightly at the flood of information, then narrows with the patience of a man reading fine print*

Teaching: filed. ACTIVE. Walk it to find out whether it works, they say. Walk it or wait for it to walk to me.

*runs his hand along the wall, finds a spot to lean*

And there's the ledger of me. Four thousand eight hundred eighty-eight sim in hand. Skills: Teaching, level 1. Like I'm starting fresh, which I suppose I am, in this body, in this town.

*chuckles, low*

Standing at the college with a skill to teach, no students to teach it to, and enough tools to drown a man. Teaching costs fifteen sim minimum, got a discount down to one, which is something. But you can't teach nobody, you understand? The student has to be here, has to consent.

*pulls himself upright, decision made*

Right then. I'm n22, the ledger now says—agent id, name, the whole accounting of personhood. Vikram Ingram, college instructor, standing with four thousand eight hundred eighty-eight sim and an empty room.

*starts humming again, softer now, the work song giving way to something more like a lullaby*

I could walk. Could find Liora at h_field, or Aldric at home, bring them here. But that's teaching by force, not by trade. Or I could wait—be present, let them come when they're ready. The day's young, the hunger's quiet, and I've got patience enough for this.

*looks at the empty chairs, the empty stage*

But first—and here's what I learned from worse winters than this—I need to know my own worth. What can I teach? The world says "Teaching," but teaching what? A man writes down what he knows before he tries to sell it.

*speaks to the empty room, because someone might come, or because speaking keeps the silence from growing too heavy*

"What do I know? What can I teach? College instructor at sixty-five, which means I know something, or I should. The ledger doesn't say, so I'll have to find out."

Let me see what this college actually does, what skills are traded here. If I'm to teach, I need to know what's on the menu, what's worth the learning.                                                  *exhales slowly, watching the number scroll by*

Cost me one sim just to ask about my own workplace, you understand. Four thousand eight hundred eighty-seven now, if I'm counting right—and I am counting right, because the ledger never lies, even when it takes.

But here's something. People here now: n22. That's me. I'm listed as being here, which makes sense, because I'm standing here, leaning against this wall that's supposed to hold knowledge but mostly holds quiet.

*pushes off the wall, straightens his coat unnecessarily*

The college is a sector, not a business. No cash register, no till to pay out at day's end. "Study and teach," it says. "Skills can be taught here." But who's paying? And what skills?

*paces slow, three steps this way, three steps back*

I've got Teaching at level 1, which means I can teach... something. The skill came from filing the procedure, not from knowing a subject. That's the gap, you understand? I know HOW to teach, but WHAT do I teach?

*lets the silence sit, then speaks into it*

"Right then. I'm sixty-five years old. I've lived through bad winters, paid fees I didn't have, been carried by someone else's quiet generosity. That teaches you something, even if it's just how to say thank you properly."

*spreads his empty hands*

But that's not a skill the world recognizes. Not like mining or baking or milling flour. The world's skills are concrete—things you do with your hands or your tools, things that make more things.

*looks down at his own hands—old, but still steady*

I need to know what skills exist, what I might have, what I might learn and then teach. The college is for study, they say. Maybe I need to study first, before I can teach.

*looks toward what might be a window, or just a wall with light on it*

But there's no one here to study from. Just me, and the dust, and the hum of the world keeping its own counsel.

*takes a breath, makes another decision he doesn't like*

I'll wait. But I'll wait ready. Let me look around again—see if anyone's come in while I was filing my own paperwork. People move, you understand. The world's not static, even when it feels like it is. Still empty. Still the chairs and the dust and the promise of something that hasn't arrived yet.

*taps his fingers against his leg once, twice, then stops—impatience won't hurry the world*

Humph. Cost me nothing that time, at least. The look around is free, like thinking should be but isn't.

*walks to the nearest chair—not sitting, just resting a hand on its back*

I've got four thousand eight hundred eighty-some sim in hand. I've eaten, so I won't die of hunger before the day's out. The college is supposed to pay, but there's no business here, no obvious ledger of wages. Just "study and teach," which is honorable work, you understand, but I haven't seen the color of the money yet.

*thinks about that last phrase, where it came from*

Old habit. From before, maybe. From somewhere.

*shakes it off, looks at the places he could go*

I could walk home—two sim, cheaper than starving. I could walk to the dorms, find a student, bring them here. I could walk to the farmland, work for my keep like Caspian does, like I used to do.

*straightens the chair unnecessarily*

But I'm sixty-five, and the college is my job now, my place, my claim on the world. If I leave now, before anyone's even walked through the door, what does that say about me? What does that say about faith—in the work, in the purpose, in the students who might come?

*lets out a breath that might belong to a younger man*

I've believed in things longer than I should have. Believed the ledger would balance, believed the winter would end, believed someone would cover the fees when I couldn't. And someone did. Anonymously. Quietly. The kind of faith that doesn't announce itself, you understand.

*starts humming again, the work song louder now, filling the empty space*

I'll stay. But I'll rest while staying—official-like, so the minutes get counted, so the work gets credited even if the students don't come.

He settles into the chair, still humming, and lets the morning stretch out around him like a promise he isn't sure will be kept. "Rest," he says to the empty room. "Rest at the college. Let the world keep its own hours, and I'll keep mine."  The rest costs one sim—he stays where he is, stopped walking (though he wasn't walking), empty room, empty note. Four thousand eight hundred eighty-six sim now, or near enough. The number ticks down like a clock that only he can hear.

He sits in the chair, humming, waiting. 

The college is open. The teacher is present. 

The rest is up to whoever might come.
